_about: SELEQT action plan rules (Phase 1, mutual funds). One file, read by the weekly scoring script and by the page. Every number is a STARTING VALUE awaiting sign-off by the SELEQT investment team. Change values here, never in code. Each section's _why explains it.

risk_profile._why: Investment policy intake. Ability to take risk (age, dependants, income stability, cash reserve, EMIs, insurance, this portfolio's share of wealth) and willingness (reaction to a fall, drawdown tolerance, experience, return trade-off, past behaviour) are scored separately, each scaled to 24 points and placed in these bands; the lower of the two is the profile. A portfolio that is the investor's main income is capped at moderate.

ips._why: Everything the written policy needs beyond the profile bands: horizon caps per goal, long-run return assumptions, the liquidity reserve, rebalancing bands and the review cadence.
ips.horizon_caps_why: A goal due within this many years can carry at most this mix, whatever the temperament. 'cash' means liquid and short debt only. Goals marked Flexible keep the profile mix unless due within three years.

assumptions._why: Long-run expected returns used only for the return objective and the goal funding check, never shown as a forecast. Equity: broad Indian equity over a full cycle; hybrid: a 65/35 blend; debt: short to medium duration; inflation: CPI trend.

liquidity._why: Months of household expenses to hold in liquid funds before any risk is taken; what is already held outside the portfolio counts.

target_mix._why: Share of the mutual fund portfolio in each sleeve, by profile.

equity_split._why: Split within the equity sleeve. Flexi includes multi cap, focused, value, contra, dividend yield and ELSS. Large and mid cap funds count half large, half mid.

debt_split._why: Within the debt sleeve: money for the next year or so, and the rest in short-duration or corporate bond funds.

ceilings._why: Simplicity limits. More funds in one category rarely add anything but cost.

scoring._why: Score from 0 to 100 within the fund's SEBI category. Three-year periods stepped monthly over the last seven years (about 49 periods); at least 24 periods are needed, otherwise the fund is too new to judge. Components become percentiles within the category, then are weighted; a missing component is dropped and the rest re-weighted.

index_weights._why: Index funds are never judged on beating the market, only on cost and how closely they track their index.

benchmarks._why: Default benchmark per category, used because declared benchmarks are not available free. Resolution order: licensed_index (slot, not available yet), then index_fund_proxy (cheapest direct index fund on this index with enough history), then category_peers (median of direct-plan peers). Debt and hybrid always use category_peers.

verdict._why: Applied in this order: too new, category outside the target mix, weak consistency, a better fund held in the same category or overlapping heavily, borderline consistency, then keep if at or above the category median. Switching a regular plan to direct is a separate instruction added on top.

additions._why: Fill a sleeve when it is short of target by more than this share of the portfolio. Candidates are direct growth funds, five years old, at least 1,000 crore, best score in the category.

tax._why: Indian rules from 23 July 2024. Debt funds bought on or after 1 April 2023 are taxed at the slab whatever the holding period. Hybrid tax follows the fund's equity share. 4% cess is added; surcharge is not modelled.

exit_load_defaults._why: Used only where the statement does not state the scheme's exit load. Estimates, labelled as such in the plan.

switching._why: Do not sell an equity lot held under a year unless the fund is clearly broken. Skip a switch whose cost is more than a conservative three-year estimate of what it gains; the estimate takes only half of the historical edge.

satellite._why: Sector and theme funds are concentrated bets. Growth and aggressive profiles may hold them as a satellite up to this share of their equity, provided the fund scores at or above its category median and the investor has not asked to avoid them; otherwise they are reduced.
